%n ammīni ea amīlūta lā banīta ša šamê u erṣeti ukellinši
#note: The sign sequence LA.BA.NI.TA has been parsed by most scholars as @i{lā banīta} “not good”, which is also followed here. The suggestion @i{lā balitta}, brought forward by @bib{Bing_JANES18@2}, cannot be maintained for reasons of graphic conventions, see @bib{RN493@29}. Perhaps one could also consider reading @akk{la ma!-ni-ta} (@i{lā manīta}), which would yield “Why did Ea disclose to humanity (such) countless amount(s) (of knowledge) about heaven and earth?”. On the question whether to understand the adjective as an attribute of @i{amīlūta} “human(ity)” or, nominalised, as the object of disclosure, see @bib{RN493@28f.} with earlier literature.

variants.reconstruction:
%n lā balṭāta ai nišī ... [...] ...
#note: One possible restoration is @akk{da-a-l[a?-t]i}, that is a f. pl. form of @i{dallu} “small, inferior”. It is favoured by Izreel (@bib{RN493@20; 32} and @bib{RN24a@44-46, 49f.} “inferior”, @bib{Izreel_GS-Kutscher@54f., 57} “poor”) as well as @bib{RN216@187} (“downtrodden”), @bib{RN164@529} (“wretched”), @bib{RN1982@258f.} (“kümmerlich”) and @bib{RN2168@60} (“poor”). @bib{RN493@32} bases his reading the transliteration given by @bib{RN1743a@968}, who apparently saw a half broken @akk{LA}, whereas none of the copies of the tablet feature the sign. Anothere possibility is to restore @akk{da-a-[ša-t]i}, i.e. a form of @i{dēšû} “flourishing”, as does von @bib{RN552@431} (“sich mehrend”). A less likely suggestion is given by @bib{Böhl.WdO2@426}: He reads the passage as @i{ai irši ṭāti} “dafür habe er [...] kein Bestechungsgeschenk”, which he takes as an idiomatic expression to the effect of “Das steht unabänderlich fest”.
